summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of recent AV graft thrombectomy was admitted with nausea, chills, and low-grade fever following a dialysis session. Initial concerns for infection were raised due to mild leukocytosis, but blood and urine cultures showed no bacterial growth, with the urine culture indicating contamination. A chest X-ray revealed subtle findings of possible mild noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and a small left pleural effusion, but no active infection. On examination, oral thrush was identified as the likely source of symptoms. The patient was started on nystatin and briefly received IV antibiotics, which were discontinued after infection was ruled out. He remained afebrile, tolerated hemodialysis, and improved clinically. He was discharged home with a 14-day course of nystatin, instructions to monitor weight, and guidance to report any swallowing difficulties.
